The limo's arrived at 6.30 and off we went with a fair sprinkling of names; Harry Wilson, Ron Roddan, Chris Brasher, Ann and Ron Wyld, Kevin Reed and so on.

It was a very moving service, with readings from Gordon's book ''Running Wild'' and addresses given by Mick Firth and Chris Brasher. Looking back to Gordon's heyday in the late 1950s we can see now what an amazing influence he had on athletics in Britain.
Other names to go on to better things were John Wilkinson and J.M.K Finley in the sprints, Angus Scott in the 880 and Chris Brasher in the 3 miles.

The emergence of Chris Brasher in this event can be noted as reaching the Olympic final. The field events, apart from a few notable exceptions such as John Savidge in the Shot, Geoff Elliott in the Pole Vault and Ron Pavitt in the High Jump, proved to be the weak link in Track & Field.

They heard addresses from Mick Firth (his close friend) and from Chris Brasher who said "Gordon was the first Briton to throw off the cloak of amateurism and put his whole being into the pursuit of excellence".
